north-guard-west.name: Nemm Hushbell
north-guard-west.description: The western entrance keeper wraps the bell because its clapper startles the creek frogs. He is tired of being called the new one.
dialogue: “I can shout farther than that bell carries. Orrit says that isn't the point.”
“Hesta wants the cloth off. I want the joint mended. We could both get what we want, if somebody would look at the joint.”
Proposed conversation: ask about the road, the watch and the bell. The repair quest and alarm response are not implemented in this preview.

north-guard-east.name: Hesta Brack
north-guard-east.description: Captain of the Stillcord. She remembers the work of bringing people down the upper road, and sometimes mistakes concern for authority.
dialogue: “You can go up. First, tell me which way you mean to come back.”
“You can leave a return plan with Vennit. Or you can tell me you would rather not. There is no toll.”
Proposed access dialogue: hear practical warnings and accept or decline the voluntary record. The existing Felling must remain reachable without a purchase or mandatory quest.

western-shopkeeper.name: Pell Drowse · The Dry Hem
western-shopkeeper.description: The guesthouse keeper collects abandoned boots and insists every pair is only waiting for its owner. He watches the courtyard for wet arrivals.
dialogue: “Dry socks first. Tell the story after you've stopped dripping on it.”
“That pair under the eave is spoken for. Most of them are. I don't mind waiting.”
Proposed service: a rented bed and clearly assigned storage. Rest, payment, rental terms and healing effects are not performed by this preview.

southwest-craftsperson.name: Orrit Coilstitch · The Long Loop
southwest-craftsperson.description: A mender who charges fairly for his time and quietly gives away fixes he thinks somebody cannot safely leave without.
dialogue: “You brought me two ends. That's nearly a rope.”
“The finished tools are for sale. The loose cord is a job. Tell me what it has to hold before I tell you what it costs.”
Proposed merchant stock is listed below using existing item blueprints. Buying, stock depletion and prices belong to native commerce; the repair and rescue-line services still need implementation.

southern-food-vendor.name: Sella Kettle · The Second Bowl
southern-food-vendor.description: The cook keeps a public table despite the cost. Every new pot is introduced as yesterday's soup.
dialogue: “Sit where you like. The tortoise has already tried that chair.”
“The cracked bowl is under the drip. Leave it there. It has finally found work it can do.”
Proposed food-and-tonic stock is listed below. Water tonic is an existing tonic, not ordinary drinking water. Purchases and any separate soup recipe still need native implementation.

east-robed-resident.name: Vennit Rusk · The Return Desk
east-robed-resident.description: A visiting Recension field scribe. His return accounts distinguish what someone saw, what someone said and what remains uncertain.
dialogue: “You told Hesta you were expected. May I enter that, or only that you passed?”
“These two visitors disagree about the upper road. I have kept both accounts and the names they allowed me to use.”
Proposed conversation: offer or withdraw testimony, read attributed accounts, or decline the record. This preview does not save testimony consent or reveal a definitive account of the Felling.

provisioners-stall.name: The Long Loop · courtyard counter
provisioners-stall.description: Ochre and green cloth shade Orrit's outside counter. The vessels and cord on display are furnishings for one shop, not duplicate free stock.
dialogue: A practical place to set down a broken thing and explain what happened.
Proposed display for Orrit's Long Loop. These are examples from the same intended merchant inventory shown on Orrit's card; the counter is not a second stocked merchant.

southern-food-stall.name: The Second Bowl · market counter
southern-food-stall.description: Violet cloth shades bowls of provisions. One corner has been wiped much more often than the others.
dialogue: Sella keeps the serving edge clear. Borrowed dishes can become a very short argument when people come back hungry.
Proposed display for The Second Bowl. Stock belongs to Sella's intended merchant inventory, not a second set of goods. No purchase or cooking transaction occurs in this preview.

north-oath-arch.name: The Stillcord entrance arch
north-oath-arch.description: Bound timber and hanging tokens frame the road north. The central way is physically open in this artwork; there are no painted gate leaves.
dialogue: A watch cord means somebody has agreed to take a shift. It comes off at supper.
The arch can be examined and its parts reviewed. A closable gate, working bell and guard access policy would require their own native states and any missing art.

central-cistern.name: Morrowfast rain cistern
central-cistern.description: A communal basin of dark rainwater, ringed with worn stone. Visitors can pass on both sides, even while somebody is filling a bucket.
dialogue: The most polished stones are at the drawing side. Nobody remembers when the bucket handle was last comfortable.
Proposed public-water interaction: a real finite liquid supply with explicit amount and purity. This art preview does not draw or drink water.

cistern-bucket.name: Communal drawing bucket
cistern-bucket.description: The bucket is older than its newest hoop. A pale worn patch shows where everybody grips it.
dialogue: A communal utensil, not an unattended shop item. Ownership and liquid capacity must be authored before native use.

southern-bread-oven.name: The low southern oven
southern-bread-oven.description: A turf-backed stone oven faces the arrival lane. Its sheltered mouth gives tired visitors somewhere obvious to stop and set a load down.
dialogue: Someone has swept the threshold and left the roof moss alone.
Baking and a distinct bread item are proposed content. The visible oven can be examined and its backing reviewed; it does not produce food in this preview.

southern-tortoise.name: Mossfoot
southern-tortoise.description: A patient yellowfoot wayfarer beside the southern oven. There is room to walk around him, although Sella says he prefers the warmest route.
dialogue: A tortoise the size of a footstool, going somewhere at its own rate.
Mossfoot is proposed as a native YellowfootWayfarer. This extracted source pose is static; movement, health, AI, pack cargo and recruitment are not inferred from the illustration.

western-bank-frog.name: Stream-bank glasspane frog
western-bank-frog.description: A pale frog has chosen a stone beside the crossing. Nemm lowers his voice here and denies doing it.
dialogue: The settlement design uses the existing GlasspaneFrog species for this creek resident. The source image supplies one visible pose.
Native animation, ecology and reactions belong to the later game binding. Removing the review sprite reveals the stone it was sitting on.

western-footbridge.name: The western footbridge
western-footbridge.description: Short boards cross the dark creek to the guesthouse back walk. The center is worn smooth; the hand-lashed posts are newer.
dialogue: A practical second route around the courtyard. A bridge-surface state must govern native travel; hiding its art in inspection is not a safe way to cross open water.

north-flower-planter.name: The entrance flower box
north-flower-planter.description: Flowers soften the waiting space between the northern houses. A planter makes a better boundary here than another spear.

northeast-herb-pot.name: The Return Desk herb pot
northeast-herb-pot.description: A narrow round pot by the witness cottage. Its flowers have survived several explanations of who was meant to water it.

northeast-offering-bowl.name: Doorstep sorting bowl
northeast-offering-bowl.description: A low bowl holds pale odds and ends beside the step. Its contents are not assigned a quest value or item blueprint yet.

western-shop-planter.name: The Dry Hem flower box
western-shop-planter.description: Pell tends this box while watching the road. He claims the flowers tell him nothing about who might be coming.

western-shop-crate.name: The Dry Hem lost-property crate
western-shop-crate.description: The small crate is meant for things left behind. Pell distinguishes abandoned property from property whose owner is late.
dialogue: Proposed storage: owned lost property with explicit contents and permissions. Reviewing the lid or hiding the crate grants no inventory items.

provisioners-water-barrel.name: The Long Loop wash barrel
provisioners-water-barrel.description: A barrel of wash water stands beside the outside counter. The cleaner-looking cup is still a workshop cup, not a promise of drinking water.

provisioners-rope-basket.name: Orrit's cord basket
provisioners-rope-basket.description: Orrit separates useful lengths from scraps here. A piece too short for one job may be exactly long enough for another.
dialogue: The cord is visible workshop material. Portable rescue rope and its uses remain proposed mechanics, so this basket does not grant an invented rope item.

southwest-handcart.name: Orrit's loaded handcart
southwest-handcart.description: Tools and bundled boards ride beside the Long Loop. The load is arranged so the things needed first are easiest to reach.
dialogue: The cart and its pictured load form one authored owner. Hauling, cargo transfer and individually taking its tools are proposed states, not current preview transactions.

southwest-sideways-barrel.name: The Long Loop spare cask
southwest-sideways-barrel.description: An empty cask lies where Orrit can brace it with a foot. Its hoops have been adjusted more recently than its staves.

southwest-worktable.name: The Long Loop outside worktable
southwest-worktable.description: A low table for cups, tools and jobs that should dry in the open air. Orrit leaves an empty patch for whatever the next visitor brings.
dialogue: “Tell me what it has to hold.”
Proposed repair and crafting service. Inspecting this table performs no repair, consumes no material and creates no item in the preview.

southwest-rope-coils.name: Orrit's paired rope coils
southwest-rope-coils.description: Two carefully laid coils keep their ends where somebody can find them. They are workshop property, not an unclaimed rescue reward.

food-stall-barrel.name: The Second Bowl counter cask
food-stall-barrel.description: A small cask sits beside the serving counter. Sella has turned its roughest stave toward the stall.

food-stall-bucket.name: The Second Bowl washing bucket
food-stall-bucket.description: A bucket waits near the counter leg. The washing water belongs here; Sella dislikes finding it beside the cistern dipper.

inn-supply-barrel.name: The Second Bowl supply barrel
inn-supply-barrel.description: A barrel of kitchen supplies stands outside the cookshop. The lid is set where Sella can reach it without putting down a bowl.

inn-empty-bucket.name: The Second Bowl spare bucket
inn-empty-bucket.description: An empty bucket waits between the supply barrel and the kitchen wall. It is small enough to disappear behind whichever job is urgent.

inn-outdoor-stove.name: The Second Bowl outside stove
inn-outdoor-stove.description: A dark pot rests on a squat stone cooking stand. The space around it has been cleared for feet, kindling and the person carrying the hot bowl.
dialogue: “Yesterday's soup,” Sella says, with the confidence of someone who has just changed it.
Cooking and a soup recipe are proposed native services. This preview shows the station and its reconstructed supporting surfaces; it does not cook or feed the player.

inn-kindling-crate.name: The Second Bowl kindling crate
inn-kindling-crate.description: Long dry pieces stand beside the outdoor stove. The narrow crate keeps them upright and off the wet ground.

inn-chopping-block.name: The Second Bowl chopping block
inn-chopping-block.description: A low block beside the kitchen has a useful flat top. The working face is small enough that it has escaped becoming a seat.

inn-sideways-cask.name: The Second Bowl spare cask
inn-sideways-cask.description: A cask lies beyond the chopping block, safely outside the door swing. Nobody calls it spare when the washing starts.

inn-northern-barrel.name: The Second Bowl covered reserve
inn-northern-barrel.description: A broad covered barrel stands above the cookshop. Its heavy-looking lid keeps the contents a matter for Sella rather than passing wildlife.
